newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares drop 1.13 pct on Iraqi tension.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares drop 1.13 pct on Iraqi tension.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell an average 1.13 percent in thin volume on Tuesday amid worries after the U.S. lauched missile attacks on military targets in southern Iraq, but recouped part of the early losses on selective buys.
Brokers said the index traded in narrow ranges in the second session with the help of support which surfaced at around 62,000 although the latest tension in Iraq haunted the market.
"The market is nervous because of the possibility that the crisis in Iraq may last longer," said Alp Tekince from Bumerang securities.
The IMKB-100 closed at 62,561.01, down 714.85 points from Monday when it shed 1.95 percent on worries following the weekend fighting in the Kurdish-held northern Iraq.
It dived 2.2 percent to a low of 61,922 at the opening on news of U.S. missile strikes before rebounding slightly.
Daily trade volume firmed to 4.9 trillion lira after sinking to 4.3 trillion lira on Monday from previous 6.2 trillion.

U.S. navy warships in the Gulf and B-52 bombers fired 27 cruise missiles on air defence and military command and communications facilities in southern Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurds in the north.
U.S. President Bill Clinton said U.S. was extending a no-fly zone in southern Iraq to restrict its ability to conduct offensive operations.
He also said a U.N. plan to allow Iraq to sell $2 billion of oil to buy food and medicines could not proceed under the currenct circumstances.
Turkey had said on Monday it would appeal to the U.N. and its Western allies to reverse a U.N. decision to delay the oil-for-food plan after the fighting began in north Iraq over the weekend.
"The market will remain tense because of the situation in Iraq, but the index is unlikely to fall below the 61,000-62,000 range," said Yalcin Arican from Hak securities.

The 85-share industrial index shed 1.19 percent to 68,464.68 and the 15-share financial index dropped 0.96 percent to 55,759.58. Of the 220 shares traded, losers sharply outdid gainers by 140 to 34 while 46 closed steady.
